newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end off highs as rand spooks market.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end off highs as rand spooks market.

text.p: South Afrian shares were buoyant at the close of a quiet Monday's trade after riding high on the back of Wall Street's gains on Friday and central bank governor Chris Stals' talk of a possible interest rate cut late in the year.

But a slip in the rand to 4.50 bid on the dollar -- its weakest level in four months -- stole some limelight from the industrials, while bullion's steady grip on $343 an ounce level failed to inspire gold shares, they added.
The industrial index ended up 42.0 points at 8,519.2, the gold index gained 5.7 points to 1,181.3 and the all-share index rose 34.2 points to 7,296.4.
Advancing issues led decliners by 226 to 139 and 148 issues were unchanged.
There were 35 new highs and 16 new lows recorded during the day. Dealers said volumes on the day were good with around 906 million rand worth of shares traded.
They said despite slight worries about the currency's stability the market would continue its recent surge and was also seen taking a cue from Wall Street's drive to scale new highs.
Wall Street firmed sharply in early New York trade on Monday.
